title: the runner on a step
line: a connector's run whose records are a results listing is found only when a row fits a person: rows under the surname fitting nobody are a none run with the reason first in its note, the rows kept on the artifact and the step planned; a connector with nothing to ask on the step's fields logs a none run with no request, the note naming the field it wanted, and the queue passes the person over

steps.say: a grandmother the file gives a name and a husband and nothing else: her baseline reviewed on those claims, and deceased on the owner's word so her searches run unattended

living.note: harness: so the steps are auto

steps.say: the death indexes asked for her surname: New Jersey's, its download standing in as the real file's header and the lines under two surnames and one more, has forty-two rows under hers and none is hers; Kentucky's is not asked, the step naming no Kentucky death

expect.why: the row's two vital-records connectors are each asked; Kentucky's has nothing to ask of a step that names no Kentucky death, and reads no file; New Jersey's rows under her surname are read and the matcher proposes none of them to anyone
the rows fit nobody: the run is a none, the reason first in its note, the whole file and the surname's rows both kept on the run
a none run leaves the step planned

steps.say: the compiled-genealogy step: each connector wants a field the step does not carry

expect.why: each connector is a none run with no request, naming the field it wanted

notes.has: it wants a birth or death year

expect.why: one log row per connector under its own source, none, no artifact, the note naming the field
run once on these fields, the step is not runnable again
